related_questions.question: What does the Secret Service investigate?

text_blocks.snippet: The Secret Service investigates crimes related to financial infrastructure and protects national leaders. Specifically, they investigate counterfeiting, cyber fraud, and other financial crimes, while also safeguarding the President, Vice President, their families, and other high-profile individuals.

list.title: Counterfeiting:
list.snippet: The Secret Service was initially established to combat the counterfeiting of U.S. currency.

list.title: Financial Institution Fraud:
list.snippet: This includes crimes like credit card fraud, bank fraud, and other fraudulent activities targeting financial institutions.

list.title: Cybercrime:
list.snippet: The agency investigates various cybercrimes such as computer fraud, online scams, and attacks on financial systems.

list.title: Access Device Fraud:
list.snippet: This encompasses crimes like credit and debit card fraud, as well as identity theft.

list.title: Business Email Compromise:
list.snippet: The Secret Service investigates scams where criminals impersonate business contacts to steal money.

list.title: National Leaders:
list.snippet: The Secret Service is responsible for protecting the President, Vice President, and their families.

list.title: Foreign Dignitaries:
list.snippet: They also protect visiting heads of state and other high-ranking foreign officials.

list.title: Major Candidates:
list.snippet: During election season, they protect presidential and vice-presidential candidates.

list.title: Former Presidents:
list.snippet: The Secret Service continues to protect former presidents and their spouses (except after remarriage).
